To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SR-BI plays an important role in the development of atherothrombotic disease.
the SR-B1 receptor is expressed in many cell types in the body and that it is important to study SR-B1 function in these cell types in order to fully understand its role in cardiovascular disease.

SR-BI in hepatocytes and platelets inhibits the development of atheromatous plaques and thrombosis respectively, while the relative contribution of SRBI in the other cell types to the pathogenesis and/or progression of atherosclerosis or cardiovascular disease remains to be determined.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the cellular functions for SR-BI in atherosclerosis, thrombosis and cardiovascular disease.
the identification of the cell type-specific roles of SR-BI and the elucidation of the underlying cellular mechanisms.
understanding the role of SR-BI on the different cells and in the different tissues in which it is expressed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SR-BI in multiple cell types and in multiple tissues contributes to the athero- and thrombo-protective effect of HDL.
SR-BI functions as a protective factor against the development of atherogenic lesions and the progression of atherosclerosis to cardiovascular disease.
SR-BI in the liver, platelets, and perhaps also in steroidogenic cells and adipocytes is atheroprotectant, whereas the impact of SR-BI on endothelial and macrophage function is less clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SR-BI in the liver, platelets and endothelium is atheroprotector, whereas SR-BI in steroidogenic cells, macrophages, adipocytes and the liver is atherogenic.

SR-BI functions in multiple cell types in a tissue-specific manner, with atherosclerosis susceptibility and cardiovascular disease risk being influenced by the SR-BI expression level and function in multiple tissues and cells.
the SR-B1 receptor plays a role in multiple cell types and that it is not just the liver that is important.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the atheroprotection afforded by SR-BI is a multifaceted process, which is likely to be the result of a combined effect of SR-BIs multiple functions in the different cells of the cardiovascular system.
SR-BI functions as a protective factor against atherosclerosis and thrombosis and that this function is mediated in part by SR-BI expressed on hepatocytes and platelets.
SR-BI function should be viewed as a multifunctional protein that can impact on multiple processes that are important in the development of atherothrombotic disease.
